text:
maria: Heads-up: running the quantized v2-7B bring-up suite across AWS/GCP/Azure and GCP p50 is ~18% higher than AWS for the same SKU/driver combo. Chart: https://dash.board/reports/sku-eval-1887 :eyes:

sam: Which SKU+driver? can you paste the env?

maria: GCP a2-highgpu, driver=535.86, CUDA=11.8, kernel=6.1. AWS p4dn (same ampere SKU), driver=535.86, CUDA=11.8, kernel=5.15. Azure ND40s_v2, driver=535.86, CUDA=11.8, kernel=5.15. All tests used quantized int8 runtime build 2026-03-17.

jordan: Are you running the same kernel cmdline (no mitigations) and same cpuset binding? NUMA or CPU steal could matter. Did you pin threads?

maria: Test command we use (identical on all clouds):
```
export MODEL=redwood-v2-7b-q8
numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./run_infer.sh --batch 1 --seq 1024 --warmup 50 --iters 200
```
No CPU governor tweaks.

nisha: Could be PCIe gen/switching or pcie ASPM differences. Also check cublas/cudnn microbench. We saw similar surface when cuBLAS used tensor cores fallback on one provider.

kevin: Do you have kernel logs showing any driver reinit or GPU resets? thermal throttles?

maria: No resets. dmesg snippet: 
```
[ 1234.5678] NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00: GPU has fallen off the bus. 
[ 1234.5680] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 31, PID=1024 ...
```
But that was from a single failed run on Azure, unrelated to the stable GCP p50 spike.

perf-bot: Auto-run summary: 1887654321 | model=redwood-v2-7b-q8 | batch=1 seq=1024 | GCP p50=123ms p95=210ms | AWS p50=104ms p95=195ms | Azure p50=106ms p95=197ms | traces=3

sam: Interesting p95s are closer. That suggests more tail variance on GCP or OS scheduling. Can you attach perf counters (sm__cycles_active, sm__inst_executed, dram__bytes.read)?

maria: Attached lightweight counters from the same run (p50 window avg): sm_active=0.78, inst_exec=4.3e9, dram_read=12GB for GCP; AWS sm_active=0.83 inst_exec=4.1e9 dram_read=11.6GB.

jordan: Lower sm_active on GCP -> either stalls or more waits (PCIe/RDMA). Are you using NCCL/peer-to-peer?

maria: Single-GPU tests, no NCCL. NVLink not present on these SKU types.

nisha: Could be PCIe link speed renegotiation. Check `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and `lspci -vvv` for Link Cap/Status. Also compare BIOS/firmware for GCP hosts — we've seen firmware ship with conservative PCIe gen.

kevin: Run a microkernel matmul and attention kernel timing to isolate if GEMM or attention kernels differ. e.g. `python tools/kernel_probe.py --kernel attention --iters 100`

maria: I'll run microbench tonight across all regions and upload results.

infra-bot: Reminder: please open an infra ticket if you want us to repro on dedicated infra instances. Ticket template: https://tickets/infra/new

sam: Also try with `--prefetch-kv=false` and `--cache-prefix=true` — we saw a regression once where prefetching caused more PCIe churn on GCP network-attached GPUs.

jordan: If the microbenchpoints match, next check CUDA driver logs for kernel fallback to legacy kernels (look for "Using fallback kernel") in our runtime logs.

maria: Agreed. Plan: 1) microbench matmul/attn on all clouds 2) collect lspci/nv-smi dmon and perf counters 3) try driver 535.104 on GCP (we're on .86) 4) test prefetch toggles. I'll post a summary tomorrow.

nisha: Assign to @maria and add me and @sam as reviewers. If it's a visible customer impact we can schedule a canary roll to a variant with prefetch disabled. :+1:

kevin: Quick note — if it's driver-specific, also test with cudnn 9 vs 8 (our lib path swap) since some int8 kernels dispatch differently.

maria: Copy. I'll include cuDNN matrix. Thanks all. :rocket:
